content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text decides a Matthew 1:16 clash by assessing the verse’s own grammatical ambiguity and noting each side’s answer rather than weighing chain against chain by footing.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings; the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"“weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse” — I weighed whether noting both sides’ answers plus the verse’s ambiguity satisfies this, versus requiring an actual comparison of the chains’ footing.","why":"The judge resolves the clash by saying Matthew 1:16’s wording admits both readings, which is verse-by-verse treatment rather than the required chain-against-chain footing analysis."}
